hints: Look at how this compound is made, think of it as two smaller molecules joining together rather than one big molecule.
Consider what $(CH_3)_3N$ has to offer with its lone pair on nitrogen, and what $AlCl_3$ is missing around aluminium.
Now count the electron pairs around Al after joining and check the shape and intermolecular forces to eliminate the other ideas.
walkthrough:
**Split the adduct into its two parts**

Think of $(CH_3)_3NAlCl_3$ as an adduct of trimethylamine, $(CH_3)_3N$, and aluminium chloride, $AlCl_3$. This helps you see where the bonding comes from.

$$ (CH_3)_3N + AlCl_3 \rightarrow (CH_3)_3NAlCl_3 $$

**Spot the donor and the acceptor**

Nitrogen in $(CH_3)_3N$ has a full octet plus one lone pair. Aluminium in $AlCl_3$ has only 3 bonds, so only 6 valence electrons and an empty orbital that can accept a pair.

$$ N: \text{ lone pair donor}, \quad Al: \text{ empty orbital acceptor} $$

**Identify the coordinate bond and complete octet**

The N lone pair is donated to Al to form an N to Al dative coordinate bond. Al now has 4 bonds, which is 8 shared electrons, so its valence shell is complete.

$$ (CH_3)_3N \rightarrow AlCl_3 $$

**Check shape and intermolecular forces**

Around Al there are 4 bonding pairs (3 x Al-Cl plus 1 x Al-N) with no lone pairs, so the arrangement is tetrahedral, not planar. There is no H bonded to N or O or F, so molecules cannot hydrogen bond to each other.

options.A: False. Hydrogen bonding needs H attached to N, O or F plus a lone pair on N, O or F of a neighbour. Here all H are in C-H methyl groups and N has no H and its lone pair is already used in bonding to Al.
options.B: False. $AlCl_3$ alone has an incomplete octet with 6 electrons, but in the adduct Al accepts the N lone pair. It then has 4 covalent bonds, giving a complete octet of 8 valence electrons.
options.C: False. Al is bonded to four atoms, three Cl and one N. With four electron pairs and no lone pair on Al, electron pair repulsion gives a tetrahedral arrangement, not trigonal planar.
options.D: Correct. The N-Al bond is a coordinate (dative covalent) bond where both shared electrons come from nitrogen. The lone pair on $(CH_3)_3N$ is donated into the vacant orbital on $AlCl_3$.
